cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: What Aren’t You Saying?
cards.instruction: Find out what someone is holding back by treating every careful answer as incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. These minutes say 'discussion of my proposal.' What did you leave out? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sign them and we can eat. Nobody wanted an awkward record.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. 'Nobody' sounds crowded. Who wanted my name out of it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did. I suggested someone else present, to save your proposal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who else? You've recorded my rescue very carefully without naming my replacement.

mechanism: A manages approval of meeting minutes while conceding privacy and speed so B reveals who lies behind careful impersonal wording.
confusable: Unlike simply correcting a document, A treats each explanation as incomplete and seeks the omitted person; borrowed authority offers a workable disclosure setting while controlling signoff.
comparison: Minutes and an unnamed replacement differ from ambiguous sibling audition feedback.
seedUse: Use D102-b minutes/nobody/proposal/presenter with S02-a adjusting the process to retain B cooperation.
